doc: Parametric constant-speed camera tracks. line: pos(t)=start+s(t)*(end-start). circle: theta deg, pos(t)=center+[radiusX*cos(theta),0,radiusZ*sin(theta)], y=center[1]. fixed: pos=position, yaw/pitch advance by *SpeedDegS with optional *MinDeg/*MaxDeg boundaries. curve: uniform Catmull-Rom spline through points[] (end tangents duplicated by clamping); a fixed 64-samples-per-segment chord table plus a monotone cubic Hermite (Fritsch-Carlson) refinement maps traveled distance to the spline parameter, pos(t) is the exact spline point (C1-smooth) at constant speedMS; lookMode path uses the analytic spline derivative. polyline: a line with multiple turns — straight segments through points[] at constant speedMS; arc length is the exact segment-length sum, pos(t) lerps inside the segment reached by traveled distance, lookMode path uses the (piecewise-constant) segment direction. spiral: f=phase01(t,turns*360/speedDegS,loopMode), theta=startAngleDeg+dir*turns*360*f with dir=+1 for cw and -1 for ccw, r=radiusStart+(radiusEnd-radiusStart)*f, y=center[1]+yStart+(yEnd-yStart)*f, pos(t)=center+[r*cos(theta),y-center[1],r*sin(theta)] — radius and height interpolate over the sweep (a circle when radiusStart=radiusEnd and yStart=yEnd). zigzag: lawnmower sweep — lanes passes across a sizeX by sizeZ rectangle centered at center, waypoints at x=center[0]+/-sizeX/2 alternating direction while z advances sizeZ/(lanes-1) per pass, joined by straight segments at constant speedMS (same segment walk as polyline). figure8: theta deg advances like circle over one full 360 deg period (angleAt with bounds startAngleDeg..startAngleDeg+/-360), pos(t)=center+[semiX*sin(theta),0,semiZ*sin(2*theta)], y=center[1] (Gerono lemniscate; closes every 360 deg). loopMode: loop wraps, pingPong mirrors at ends, once stops at end. Orientation: lookAt point when lookMode is center|point|path; lookMode "normal" looks along N=normalize(cross(T,up)) with T the travel tangent (reversed on the pingPong return leg, same rule as path) and up=+Y, so N is horizontal and perpendicular to T (T parallel to up falls back to cross(T,+Z), then cross(T,+X)); normalDirection "forward"|"backward" selects +N|-N; else fixed yaw/pitch (YXZ Euler, +Y up, pitch positive = up). Units: meters / degrees / seconds. Coordinates are the glTF file own world space (identity transform). Per-model flags: fogon, nighton, flashlighton (booleans, derived from the World & Weather panel in v1) ride with each models[] entry for the consuming program; the full world env also rides as models[].env { pair:[A,B] (MAP_EFFECTS_INFOS indices 0..20), weatherTarget 0..8 (sharedFunc_800D0B18 arg), bootWeather -1..6, lensFlare 0..5, flashlightOn, psxWobble, dither, particles, engine, animsDemo (v13.2: the cutscene/event-gated SH1X drivers play — the PoC v32.2 engine parses it; the wallpaper demo scenes set it per camdat) }. durationSec is informational (one playback cycle). PER-TRACK WEATHER (v12): models[].tracks[].weatherTarget (optional, 0..8, strict number) is the weather THE TRACK carries — the sharedFunc_800D0B18 argument, resolved track > models[].env.weatherTarget when present. Consumers apply it through the engine’s own 512-tick sine cross-fade (the authentic runtime transition); the CamTrack v12 EDITOR previews it instantly (no cross-fade). DAY/NIGHT ENVIRONMENTS (v13): models[].env.dayEnv and models[].env.nightEnv (optional, 0..20, MAP_EFFECTS_INFOS indices) are the scene’s Auto-Mode presets — the environments the wallpaper applies by daylight phase (sun-time or the device schedule); models[].tracks[].envDay / models[].tracks[].envNight (optional, 0..20) override them per track (resolved track > model; absent = inherit the model preset, which itself falls back to the base env pair slot A). The wallpaper app layers them under its own preferences (app override > camdat track > camdat model > app custom mapping > the authentic defaults 1/3). The CamTrack v13 EDITOR previews the phase presets INSTANTLY through its session-only Day/Night lens (applied as the pair {N,N}, never serialized); the ENGINE transitions day/night through its own environment paths.
